title: An Improved Method for the Preparation of Type I Collagen From Skin
protocol: Equilibrate all reagents to 4°C prior to use.
Rinse dermal sample in ice-cold dH2O and remove any wool, fur, or hair with depilatory cream.
Scrape the sample clean of connective tissue and fat with a single-edge razor blade.
Slice the skin sample into 1 cm x 1 cm pieces with a single-edge razor blade.
Weigh out 5 g of sample per 50 ml conical tube and add 30 ml of ice-cold 0.5 M sodium acetate.
Mix tubes for 1 min at the 6 m/sec setting using a 50 ml tube adaptor in the bench-top homogenizer.
Discard supernatant and repeat for a total of 7 sodium acetate wash cycles.
Rinse the sample in ice-cold dH2O and mix once to remove residual sodium acetate.
Compress the sample against the side of the tube with a spatula to remove excess liquid and transfer to a fresh 50 ml conical tube.
Wash the sample twice in 2 ml/g 0.075 M sodium citrate buffer for 1 min at 6 m/sec in the bench-top homogenizer compressing the sample after each wash.
Discard supernatant after each wash cycle.
Add a fresh 2 ml/g aliquot of 0.075 M sodium citrate buffer to the sample.
Perform 6 sequential 1 min, 6 m/sec bench-top homogenizer mix cycles without removing the buffer between each cycle.
Transfer the thick, clear supernatant to a collection tube.
Add an additional 1 ml/g of 0.075 M sodium citrate buffer to the sample.
Agitate the sample using a bench-top homogenizer for one final cycle.
Centrifuge the collection tube at 3,200 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant to the top compartment of a 100,000 molecular weight cut off centrifugal filter device.
Centrifuge at 3,200 x g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the purified COL1 from the upper compartment to a clean conical tube.
Store the purified COL1 at 4 °C.
